title: Disentangling Identity-Composition Drift from Within-Identity Embedding Drift in Biometric Representation Systems
research_questions: How do changes in identity composition affect global embedding distributions?
Can within-identity embedding distribution changes be detected independently of identity-composition changes?
How effectively can global and identity-conditioned monitoring distinguish mechanisms?
How do detection performance and false alarms change when both mechanisms occur simultaneously?

scenario_design.description: Stable identity composition and conditional distributions.
Changed identity proportions with original embeddings.
Stable identity proportions with low-illumination embedding variants.
Changed identity proportions and low-illumination embedding variants.

key_findings.evidence: Global Euclidean and Mahalanobis detectors detected all 11 post-change windows in C1 and C3 at the 5% threshold.
key_findings.interpretation: The global embedding distribution was sensitive to the constructed identity-composition changes.

key_findings.evidence: C2 produced greater identity-level displacement than C0, with a mean paired difference of 0.091008 and Holm-adjusted p-value of 0.001953.
key_findings.interpretation: The low-illumination condition produced measurable within-identity embedding displacement.

key_findings.evidence: C3 versus C1 had a positive mean paired difference of 0.036232, but its Holm-adjusted p-value was 0.064453.
key_findings.interpretation: The additional within-identity effect under the combined condition was not statistically significant after Holm correction.

key_findings.evidence: The vector decomposition reconstructed the total mean shift with maximum numerical error 8.85e-17.
key_findings.interpretation: The decomposition is numerically consistent, but its estimated components include sampling noise.

limitations: The experiment uses a filtered LFW-derived subset containing 13 identities.
Identity 14 accounts for approximately 56.69% of the original paired cohort.
Bootstrap sampling with replacement means repeated draws are not independent images.
The evaluation contains only 22 windows per scenario.
Calibration thresholds are based on 181 calibration observations and bootstrap windows.
The within-identity drift scenario uses low-illumination embedding variants.
The post-change samples are independently resampled rather than strictly paired image observations.
The statistical analysis uses only 13 identity-level paired observations.
The results do not establish real-world biometric recognition accuracy.
The results do not establish operational fairness or deployment readiness.
The experiment does not establish causal isolation of drift mechanisms.
